request: Create a small, playable Sky Steps checkpoint parkour game for one player on desktop and touch. Build one coherent short course with three ordered checkpoints, a moving-platform crossing, a clearly marked fall hazard, and a finish. Players must physically traverse it; touching a later checkpoint early must not skip progress. Reaching a checkpoint shows visible activation animation and synchronized confirmation sound. Falling returns the player to the last valid checkpoint without losing progress. Show the current checkpoint and elapsed run time, then a completion result and deliberate replay control. Search Marketplace first for reusable checkpoint, moving-platform and course components, preserving useful existing behavior, visuals, motion and media. Inspect what is included and integrate missing rules rather than replacing working components wholesale. Use Marketplace audio and verify it actually plays. If a suitable component cannot be imported faithfully, record that capability gap. Use compact readable geometry and comfortable jumps; choose reasonable style and layout yourself. No multiplayer, saving, purchases or sprawling map. Success needs native traversal, ordered progression, moving-platform behavior, fall recovery, finish/replay and legible desktop/touch UI. A decorative obstacle scene or a timer alone is insufficient.

playerExperience.title: Sky Steps: Three-Checkpoint Sprint
playerExperience.summary:
A compact solo sky-parkour run contained under the supplied namespace. The course begins on a safe floating spawn island with a bright Start pad, a visible chain of floating steps, three numbered checkpoint beacons, a moving-platform crossing, a high-contrast fall zone below, and a finish arch visible in the distance. In the first minute, the player sees the route and HUD immediately, steps onto Start to begin the timer, learns the comfortable jump spacing, reaches Checkpoint 1, and receives a beacon activation animation plus synchronized Marketplace confirmation sound. The route then leads through the moving-platform crossing to Checkpoint 2, an ascending final step sequence to Checkpoint 3, and the finish.

Progress is server-authoritative and ordered: only the next checkpoint activates, while touching later checkpoints early has no effect. Falling into the marked hazard or below the course returns the character to the last valid checkpoint without resetting checkpoint progress or elapsed time. The finish only accepts a player who has activated all three checkpoints. Completion freezes the result time and presents a deliberate Replay button; replay resets the run, progress, timer, character position, checkpoint visuals, and moving-course state where required.

Assumptions chosen from the user's permission to choose reasonable style and layout: the timer starts on physical contact with the Start pad; checkpoint order is Start → 1 → 2 → 3 → Finish; horizontal jumps generally remain around 4–6 studs with broad landing surfaces; the moving platform uses a short, readable route with safe boarding areas; replay is never automatic. The experience has no persistence, purchases, competitive systems, or multiplayer-facing features. Internally, player state is still indexed and cleaned per UserId so respawn and server lifecycle behavior remain safe.

Marketplace checkpoint, moving-platform, and complete obby/course components must be searched and inspected before implementation decisions. Useful verified geometry, scripts, motion, animation, and media will be retained. Unsupported scripts, missing dependencies, failed audio playback, or behavior that cannot be imported faithfully are explicit capability gaps and do not authorize an unverified procedural substitute.
playerExperience.visualDirection:
Use a clean, optimistic high-altitude aesthetic with compact floating islands and a clearly readable forward route. Main traversable surfaces use pale cloud-white and cool cyan materials; structural undersides use deeper blue-violet tones to give each island a designed silhouette. Checkpoints are tall numbered beacon assemblies with dormant cyan rings and a vivid green-white activated state. The finish is a larger gold-white arch that remains visually distinct from checkpoints.

Compose the course as one shallow rising arc rather than a sprawling straight line. From spawn, the player should see Checkpoint 1 in the near foreground, the moving-platform crossing and Checkpoint 2 at mid-distance, then Checkpoint 3 and the finish as elevated focal points. Keep landing surfaces broad, edge profiles crisp, and decorative elements away from jump paths.

The fall hazard is unmistakable: a broad red-magenta warning volume or plane sits below the course, with luminous warning strips and downward chevrons at exposed transition edges. It must contrast strongly with the cool safe-route palette and remain legible without relying on text alone.

Checkpoint activation should be observable from the player camera: illuminate or recolor the beacon, expand or pulse a ring, and briefly emphasize the checkpoint number. Preserve an imported component's verified animation if it provides equivalent feedback. The confirmation sound begins in the same activation phase as the visible response. Later checkpoints remain visibly dormant until their turn.

The HUD is compact and readable on desktop and touch: a top-center checkpoint label such as “Checkpoint 1 / 3,” a large tabular elapsed time beneath it, and restrained status messaging. On completion, show a centered result card with the final time and a generously sized Replay button suitable for touch. Use strong contrast, safe-area-aware margins, rounded panels, and text sizing that remains readable on narrow phone screens. Do not cover the central jump view during active play.

playerExperience.assetStrategy:
Begin with complete reusable Model searches for checkpoint systems, moving-platform systems, and compact sky-obstacle courses, because these may include the requested geometry, scripts, motion, activation animation, reset hooks, and sound references. Inspect candidate hierarchies and source code, reject arbitrary HTTP or numeric require dependencies, identify unsupported serialization, and test existing behavior before assigning glue scripts or designing replacements. Preserve useful verified behavior and media rather than rebuilding imported components wholesale.

Audio remains a separate required asset obligation even if a checkpoint component includes it. Prefer captured audio from a retained checkpoint component, then search Marketplace separately if no suitable included cue exists. The chosen sound must retain provenance and pass loading, playback, and listening checks. Standalone animation retrieval is not assumed; checkpoint animation should come from an inspectable Model when available. Any necessary authored visual tween or integration may only be decided after inspection establishes that equivalent reusable behavior is absent and the asset pipeline records the sourcing result. Import failures, hidden dependencies, unsupported behavior, or failed audio verification must be reported as capability gaps rather than treated as authorization for a procedural substitute.

need.role: Reusable checkpoint system or obby checkpoint component that may supply beacon geometry, touch behavior, activation animation, progression interfaces, and embedded confirmation media for the three ordered checkpoints.
need.constraints: Must be inspectable and retainable inside Workspace/Forge_c405e7e9b70b. Prefer a compact component with source-visible behavior, numbered or easily distinguishable checkpoints, clear dormant and active states, and no datastore, monetization, admin, or competitive dependencies. Audit all scripts and dependencies; ordered progression, server validation, respawn integration, animation, and media claims require native verification. Unsupported serialization or hidden dependencies are capability gaps, not permission to rebuild it procedurally.

intent.experienceRole: Provides the recurring progression landmark and immediate reward feedback that makes the short parkour run understandable and satisfying.
intent.interaction: The player physically touches the next valid checkpoint; the server accepts it, the beacon visibly activates, confirmation audio begins, and the new location becomes the fall-recovery destination. Early and repeated touches produce no progress reward.

7: local function SafeWaitForChild(ParentObject, ChildName, TimeoutDuration)
8: 	-- Safely waits for a child instance to be available in the hierarchy
9: 	-- Useful for handling replication delays and network latency issues
10: 
11: 	if ParentObject == nil then
12: 		error("Parent object cannot be nil", 2)
13: 	end
14: 	if type(ChildName) ~= "string" then
15: 		error("Child name must be a string value", 2)
16: 	end
17: 
18: 	local TargetChild = ParentObject:FindFirstChild(ChildName)
19: 	local StartTime = tick()
20: 	local TimeoutWarning = false
21: 
22: 	while TargetChild == nil and ParentObject ~= nil do
23: 		RunService.Heartbeat:Wait()
24: 		TargetChild = ParentObject:FindFirstChild(ChildName)
25: 		if TimeoutWarning == false and StartTime + (TimeoutDuration or 5) <= tick() then
26: 			TimeoutWarning = true
27: 			warn("Potential infinite yield detected in SafeWaitForChild(" .. ParentObject:GetFullName() .. ", " .. ChildName .. ")")
28: 			if TimeoutDuration then
29: 				return ParentObject:FindFirstChild(ChildName)
30: 			end
31: 		end
32: 	end
33: 
34: 	if ParentObject == nil then
35: 		warn("Parent object no longer exists during SafeWaitForChild operation")
36: 	end
37: 
38: 	return TargetChild
39: end

160: function TextureConfigurationSystem.CFG(ConfigurationContainer)

163: 
164: 	if ConfigurationCache[ConfigurationContainer] then

176: 			if type(ConfigurationKey) ~= "string" then

183: 				return function(ValueType, ConfigurationData)
184: 					local TargetObject

189: 							print("[TextureConfigurationSystem] - Type mismatch detected: " .. TargetObject.ClassName .. " replaced with " .. ValueType)
190: 							TargetObject:Destroy()
191: 							TargetObject = nil
192: 						end
193: 					else
194: 						error("[TextureConfigurationSystem] - Invalid configuration data provided", 2)
195: 					end
196: 
197: 					if TargetObject == nil then
198: 						local NewInstance = Instance.new(ValueType)
199: 						ApplyInstanceProperties(NewInstance, ConfigurationData)
200: 						NewInstance.Parent = ConfigurationContainer
201: 					end
202: 				end
203: 			elseif NormalizedKey == "get" or NormalizedKey == "getvalue" then
204: 				return function(ObjectName)
205: 					return LocateConfigurationObject(ObjectName)
206: 				end
207: 			elseif NormalizedKey == "getcontainer" then
208: 				return function(ContainerName)
209: 					return LocateConfigurationObject(ContainerName)

212: 				local ConfigObject = LocateConfigurationObject(ConfigurationKey)

223: 				if ConfigObject and ValidConfigurationTypes[ConfigObject.ClassName] then

225: 				else
226: 					error("[TextureConfigurationSystem] - Configuration access error for: " .. ConfigurationKey, 2)
227: 				end

229: 		end,

231: 		__newindex = function(_, PropertyName, NewValue)

94: 	-- Creates a new texture asset with specified configuration
95: 	local textureData = SUPPORTED_TEXTURE_TYPES[assetType]
96: 	if not textureData then
97: 		error("Unsupported texture type: " .. tostring(assetType), 2)
98: 	end
99: 
100: 	local newAsset = Instance.new(textureData.Class)
101: 	return ApplyProperties(newAsset, configuration or textureData.DefaultProperties)
102: end

104: -- Texture analysis and optimization functions
105: function TextureConfiguration.AnalyzeTextureUsage(gameRoot)
106: 	-- Analyzes all textures in the game and returns usage statistics
107: 	local textureStats = {
108: 		totalTextures = 0,
109: 		byType = {},
110: 		memoryUsage = 0,
111: 		missingTextures = 0
112: 	}
113: 
114: 	local function scanHierarchy(object)
115: 		if SUPPORTED_TEXTURE_TYPES[object.ClassName] then
116: 			textureStats.totalTextures = textureStats.totalTextures + 1
117: 			textureStats.byType[object.ClassName] = (textureStats.byType[object.ClassName] or 0) + 1
118: 
119: 			-- Check for missing texture references
120: 			if object:IsA("Decal") and object.Texture == "" then
121: 				textureStats.missingTextures = textureStats.missingTextures + 1
122: 			end
123: 		end
124: 
125: 		for _, child in ipairs(object:GetChildren()) do
126: 			scanHierarchy(child)
127: 		end
128: 	end
129: 
130: 	scanHierarchy(gameRoot)
131: 	return textureStats
132: end
133: 
134: function TextureConfiguration.GenerateMissingTextures(parentContainer, textureMap)
135: 	-- Generates placeholder textures for missing texture references
136: 	local generatedCount = 0
137: 
138: 	for textureName, textureConfig in pairs(textureMap) do
139: 		local existingTexture = parentContainer:FindFirstChild(textureName)
140: 
141: 		if not existingTexture then
142: 			local newTexture = CreateTextureAsset(textureConfig.Type, textureConfig.Properties)
143: 			newTexture.Name = textureName
144: 			newTexture.Parent = parentContainer
145: 			generatedCount = generatedCount + 1
146: 		elseif existingTexture.ClassName ~= textureConfig.Type then
147: 			warn("[TextureConfiguration] - Texture type mismatch for '" .. textureName .. "'. Expected: " .. textureConfig.Type .. ", Found: " .. existingTexture.ClassName)
148: 		end
149: 	end
150: 
151: 	print("[TextureConfiguration] - Generated " .. generatedCount .. " missing textures")
152: 	return generatedCount
153: end

155: function TextureConfiguration.CreateTextureLayer(layerName, parentContainer)
156: 	-- Creates an organized container for texture assets
157: 	local textureLayer = parentContainer:FindFirstChild(layerName)
158: 
159: 	if not textureLayer then
160: 		textureLayer = Instance.new("Folder")
161: 		textureLayer.Name = layerName
162: 		textureLayer.Archivable = false
163: 		textureLayer.Parent = parentContainer
164: 	end
165: 
166: 	return textureLayer
167: end

169: -- Main texture configuration interface
170: function TextureConfiguration.GetTextureManager(textureContainer)
171: 	-- Returns a managed interface for texture configuration operations
172: 	if TextureCache[textureContainer] then
173: 		return TextureCache[textureContainer]
174: 	end
175: 
176: 	local textureManager = {}
177: 
178: 	local function FindTexture(textureName)
179: 		return textureContainer:FindFirstChild(textureName)
180: 	end
181: 
182: 	setmetatable(textureManager, {
183: 		__index = function(_, operation)
184: 			local operationLower = operation:lower()
185: 
186: 			if operationLower == "addtexture" or operationLower == "create" then
187: 				return function(textureType, configuration)
188: 					local textureName = configuration and configuration.Name
189: 
190: 					if not textureName or type(textureName) ~= "string" then
191: 						error("[TextureConfiguration] - Texture configuration must include a valid Name property", 2)
192: 					end
193: 
194: 					local existingTexture = FindTexture(textureName)
195: 					if existingTexture and existingTexture.ClassName ~= textureType then
196: 						warn("[TextureConfiguration] - Replacing existing texture '" .. textureName .. "' of type " .. existingTexture.ClassName .. " with new type " .. textureType)
197: 						existingTexture:Destroy()
198: 						existingTexture = nil
199: 					end
200: 
201: 					if not existingTexture then
202: 						local newTexture = CreateTextureAsset(textureType, configuration)
203: 						newTexture.Parent = textureContainer
204: 					end
205: 				end
206: 
207: 			elseif operationLower == "gettexture" or operationLower == "find" then
208: 				return function(textureName)
209: 					return FindTexture(textureName)
210: 				end
211: 
212: 			elseif operationLower == "getlayer" then
213: 				return function(layerName)
214: 					return textureContainer:FindFirstChild(layerName)
215: 				end
216: 
217: 			else
218: 				-- Direct texture property access
219: 				local texture = FindTexture(operation)
220: 				if texture and SUPPORTED_TEXTURE_TYPES[texture.ClassName] then
221: 					return texture
222: 				else
223: 					error("[TextureConfiguration] - Texture '" .. operation .. "' not found or unsupported type", 2)
224: 				end
225: 			end
226: 		end,
227: 
228: 		__newindex = function(_, textureName, propertyTable)
229: 			local texture = FindTexture(textureName)
230: 			if texture and SUPPORTED_TEXTURE_TYPES[texture.ClassName] then
231: 				ApplyProperties(texture, propertyTable)
232: 			else
233: 				error("[TextureConfiguration] - Cannot configure non-existent texture: " .. textureName, 2)
234: 			end
235: 		end
236: 	})
237: 
238: 	TextureCache[textureContainer] = textureManager
239: 	return textureManager
240: end

242: -- Quality optimization functions
243: function TextureConfiguration.OptimizeTextures(textureContainer, qualityPreset)
244: 	-- Applies optimization settings to all textures in container
245: 	local preset = TEXTURE_PRESETS[qualityPreset] or TEXTURE_PRESETS.Medium
246: 	local optimizedCount = 0
247: 
248: 	local function processTexture(texture)
249: 		if texture:IsA("Decal") then
250: 			-- Apply decal-specific optimizations
251: 			texture.ZIndex = preset.Resolution / 256
252: 		elseif texture:IsA("Texture") then
253: 			-- Apply texture-specific optimizations
254: 			texture.StudsPerTileU = math.max(1, preset.Resolution / 512)
255: 			texture.StudsPerTileV = math.max(1, preset.Resolution / 512)
256: 		end
257: 
258: 		optimizedCount = optimizedCount + 1
259: 	end
260: 
261: 	local function scanTextures(object)
262: 		if SUPPORTED_TEXTURE_TYPES[object.ClassName] then
263: 			processTexture(object)
264: 		end
265: 
266: 		for _, child in ipairs(object:GetChildren()) do
267: 			scanTextures(child)
268: 		end
269: 	end
270: 
271: 	scanTextures(textureContainer)
272: 	print("[TextureConfiguration] - Optimized " .. optimizedCount .. " textures with " .. qualityPreset .. " preset")
273: 	return optimizedCount
274: end
